page: Amazon Web Services r7gd.xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine operating on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by an AWS Neoverse-V1 ARMv8 processor featuring four dedicated physical cores running at 2.6 GHz with single-threaded execution per core. The hardware configuration includes 32.0 GB of system memory, providing an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is bundled directly via an integrated 237 GB local NVMe SSD instance store volume, and network connectivity is supported by a 2 Gbps baseline bandwidth. Discrete graphics accelerators are not included in this configuration.

Benchmarking reveals distinct performance characteristics, led by a strong memory subsystem scoring 2770.8 in PassMark, placing it in the upper quartile. Memory bandwidth delivers 98.01 GB/sec on large uncached reads and 386.23 GB/sec on cached reads. General compute throughput remains in the median range, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 4844.0 and stress-ng multi-core metric of 6112.65. Application tests demonstrate 6.96 million Redis SET operations per second and static web throughput of 8.32 GB/sec. Lower relative performance is observed in extended vector instructions, compression decompress pipelines, and local LLM inference tasks.

From an efficiency perspective, the ARM architecture provides dedicated per-core resources and high memory density without the overhead of hyperthreading. The main architectural limitation is the ephemeral nature of the bundled NVMe instance storage and lower throughput in floating-point or heavy cryptographic instructions. These specifications make the r7gd.xlarge suitable for memory-heavy production environments, including Redis or Memcached instances, relational database caching tiers, temporary ETL scratch storage, and low-latency API serving.
description: Amazon Web Services r7gd.xlarge is a memory-optimized server powered by an ARMv8 AWS Neoverse-V1 processor with 4 dedicated cores clocked at 2.6 GHz. Built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the platform provides 32.0 GB of RAM alongside an integrated 237 GB local NVMe SSD and a 2 Gbps baseline network interface. It excludes hardware GPU accelerators. The instance achieves a top-tier PassMark memory score and handles 6.96 million Redis SET operations per second, supported by uncached read bandwidth of 98.01 GB/sec. Standard compute benchmarks such as Geekbench place the system in the median tier, whereas complex vector execution and text generation benchmarks demonstrate reduced throughput. With 8.0 GB of memory per vCPU and fast ephemeral local storage, the instance fits in-memory databases, caching systems, and read-heavy operational workloads requiring direct local scratch space.
